title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech pushed next-month rate-hike odds to ~60% (from 35%); 2-yr Treasury yield rose to 4.35%, gold fell >3% to ~$4,509, and the S&P 500 (-0.25%) and Nasdaq (-0.5%) slipped Friday, trimming Thursday's Nvidia-fueled rally
Markets: Agricultural commodities extended a sharp run — wheat up ~51% year-to-date (+10% this week), corn +22% YTD, soybeans +22% YTD
Companies: Chevron and Halliburton are reportedly near deals to expand Venezuelan oil operations as the Trump administration negotiates a U.S. ownership stake in Venezuela's oil reserves

Companies: Meta reached a multistate settlement over claims Facebook/Instagram harmed children, forcing product changes and billions in penalties after Congress's Kids Online Safety Act repeatedly stalled

Companies: Tyson Foods and JBS shares fell after Trump said he's drafting rules to let farmers/ranchers process their own meat, threatening processors' business model; Broadcom, Palo Alto Networks, Dell and HPE report earnings next week, with the August jobs report due Friday Sept. 4
Macro/Policy: A federal judge struck down the Pentagon's blacklisting of Anthropic as a 'supply-chain risk' in its dispute over military use of Claude; the government is expected to appeal

Macro/Policy: Oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz remain about two-thirds of pre-war levels per Goldman Sachs; Trump plans to meet refiners and fuel retailers next week over high gas prices ahead of the midterms
